entities.summary: Figure 4 provides an overview of the findings on source address validation (SAV) deployment for packets both outbound from and inbound to the measured network, for the year ending August 1, 2019. entities.name: figure 5

The figure indicates that there is no meaningful correlation between prefix age and spoofability. The hypothesis that older networks are more mature and have better hygiene was not supported by the data, as no significant relationship was found between the age of a prefix and the probability of SAV deployment.

entities.name: figure 6
entities.summary: Figure 6 displays the cumulative fraction of IPv4 /24 prefixes and ASes that reported measurements in 20 or more weeks between May 2016 and August 2019. The data shows that even with the daemonized Spoofer client, 44% of the IPv4 /24 prefixes and 32% of the ASes reported measurements in only a single week. This sparsity complicates inferences of remediation, as it is difficult to determine whether a network has deployed SAV or if the first tested prefix still permits spoofing.

entities.name: figure 7
entities.summary: Figure 7 plots the per-prefix spoofability recall and precision of a model as a function of the month that splits the training from the test data. The data shows that as the system has accumulated more tests, the model's predictive recall has increased significantly, from around 20% in May 2016 to more than 80% for IPv6 in August 2019, but only 50-70% for IPv4. Similarly, the model's precision has increased significantly in the last year, with IPv6 predictions outperforming IPv4 predictions. The model's performance is attributed to the topological characteristics in the observed data rather than random guesses based on the overall prior spoofing probability.

entities.name: figure 8

entities.name: figure 9
